extra.message: DOM-based stored XSS. Incoming STOMP websocket chat messages (JSON.parse(incoming.body), line 49) contain content authored by other users. chatMessage.author.name and chatMessage.message are concatenated into an HTML string and assigned to p.innerHTML with no encoding or sanitization. A malicious user can send a chat message such as '' that executes as JavaScript in every recipient's browser when the chat panel renders it, enabling cookie/session theft and actions on behalf of the victim. Text content should be assigned via textContent or React JSX (auto-escaped), not innerHTML.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: DOM-based XSS via jQuery HTML injection. showContactDetails() passes user.emailAddress to jQuery's replaceWith(). jQuery parses the argument as HTML when it begins with '<', and user.emailAddress is fully attacker-controlled through the unvalidated 'Mail address' registration field (Register.js, name='emailAddress', plain text input with no format validation). An attacker who registers with emailAddress '' achieves script execution in the browser of any user who clicks 'Click to show contact' on the Users page. Insert the value as text (e.g. via .text()) instead of replaceWith().

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: XSS via untrusted URL in anchor href. The profile popup renders <a href={user.webPageUrl}>, where webPageUrl is fully controlled by another user through the unvalidated 'Your webpage' registration field (Register.js, free-text input, no scheme validation). React 15.6 does not block javascript: URLs (blocking was only added much later), so registering webPageUrl='javascript:alert(document.cookie)' makes the 'Go to Xs web page' link execute attacker-supplied JavaScript when a victim clicks it. The URL must be validated to allow only http/https schemes before rendering it in an href.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Reverse tabnabbing. The external link to user.webPageUrl (an attacker-controllable URL set at registration) is opened with target="_blank" but without rel="noopener noreferrer". The opened page receives a window.opener reference to this application's tab and can navigate it to a phishing page while the user is looking at the new tab, enabling credential theft. Add rel="noopener noreferrer" to the anchor.

cwe: CWE-1022: Use of Web Link to an Untrusted Site with target=_blank

extra.message: Hardcoded credentials. The STOMP-over-SockJS websocket connection to the backend is authenticated with the hardcoded username/password pair 'asdf'/'were' embedded in client-side source. Because this code is shipped to every browser, the credentials are trivially extractable from the JS bundle and anyone can connect to the broker and subscribe to '/user/queue/notifications', defeating the websocket authentication.

Cleartext transmission of sensitive information. All backend communication is directed at hardcoded plain-HTTP endpoints (http://35.204.241.43:31337/ and .../rest/). The login POST (Login.js) carries the user's username and password in the request body, and all requests use credentials:'include', sending session cookies. Both are transmitted unencrypted and can be intercepted/read/modified by a network attacker (man-in-the-middle). The backend URLs must use HTTPS.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Login CSRF. The login form is submitted as a cross-origin-capable 'simple' request (POST with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded, credentials:'include') with no anti-CSRF token, same-origin check, or one-time request token. A malicious website can silently submit a hidden login form that logs the victim into an attacker-controlled account (login CSRF), enabling subsequent impersonation and capture of data the victim enters. A CSRF token (e.g. synchronizer token or double-submit cookie) and SameSite cookies are required.

CSRF on a state-changing endpoint. sendChatToBackend() issues an authenticated PUT to messages/chat with credentials:'include' (session cookies attached) and no anti-CSRF token or origin validation anywhere in the client. If the backend's CORS policy is permissive (or via the other cookie-bearing endpoints), a malicious page can cause an authenticated user's browser to send forged chat messages on the victim's behalf. State-changing requests require an anti-CSRF token and origin checks.

State-changing operation performed via GET. Logout is triggered with a GET request to the backend 'logout' endpoint with credentials:'include'. GET-based state changes are CSRF-able with simple cross-site requests (e.g. ) and may also be triggered by link prefetchers or browser caches, allowing an attacker to forcibly log a victim out (denial of service / session disruption). Logout should be a POST with an anti-CSRF token.

Insecure storage of sensitive information. The full login response (the authenticated user's profile object) is persisted in window.localStorage under 'loggedInUser'. localStorage is readable by any script running on the page and persists indefinitely, so in combination with the DOM XSS vulnerabilities in Users.js an attacker can exfiltrate the victim's stored user data. Sensitive user/session data should be kept in non-script-accessible storage (httpOnly cookie) or in memory only.

cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Improper input validation in URL construction. user.name, which is attacker-controlled via the registration form and never validated/normalized, is concatenated directly into the request query string ('messages/chat?otherUser=' + user.name) without encodeURIComponent(). A name containing '&', '=' or '#' injects or corrupts query parameters of the backend request (e.g. adding extra parameters or truncating the value), causing the chat history request to be issued for a different target than displayed. Use encodeURIComponent() on all user-controlled URL components.
